name: OR-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by six points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Val Hoyle has a large fundraising edge and outside support
Prediction markets price Hoyle around 94% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Hoyle: a D+6 district, incumbency, and a better than two-to-one fundraising advantage over Monique DeSpain, with markets pricing her near certain to win. With no polls to contradict that picture, the forecast stays safely Democratic, trimmed slightly toward the market's more conservative read.
model.watch: Any late polling showing DeSpain within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Hoyle, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Val Hoyle seeks a second term in a southwestern Oregon district that leans Democratic by six points. She has out-raised Republican Monique DeSpain by a wide margin, holds a cash advantage, and benefits from outside spending on her behalf, while DeSpain has run a modestly funded campaign. A minor independent is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which price Hoyle's chances at roughly 94 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the expected margin somewhat narrower than the raw fundamentals would suggest given the market's read.
